text:
They said
        in Antiquity that poetry
is a stairway to God. Perhaps it is not
        so
when you read me now. But I knew it the day
that through you I found
        my voice again, dissolved
in a flock of clouds and unruly
goats, which from a crag were stripping the leaves
from the plum tree and
        the cattail, and the thinned faces
of the moon and sun were melting;
the engine was broken and an arrow
of blood on a rock
        marked
the road to Aleppo.

translation.title: Syria
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the Syrian landscape, the damaged engine, and the blood arrow as the route back to voice.
